questions.q: In CUDA terminology, what is the "host"?
options: The GPU and its memory
The CPU and its RAM
The CUDA driver software
A remote server running the training job
questions.explain: The host refers to the CPU and its RAM, as distinct from the device (the GPU and its own memory).

questions.q: What does the __global__ keyword mark in CUDA C++?
options: A variable that is globally accessible from every thread
A function that is callable from host code but executes on the device across many threads
A memory allocation that spans the entire GPU
A header file that must be included in every CUDA program
questions.explain: __global__ marks a kernel: a function callable from the host that runs on the device, executed by many threads simultaneously.

questions.q: Why must data be explicitly copied between host and device memory in CUDA?
options: Because host and device memory are physically separate pools connected by PCIe or NVLink
Because CUDA does not support any form of memory allocation
Because GPUs cannot store data persistently
Because all CUDA programs run entirely on the CPU
questions.explain: Host RAM and device (GPU) memory are physically separate, connected by PCIe or NVLink, so data must be explicitly transferred with calls like cudaMemcpy.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the five basic steps in a CUDA C++ program?
options: Launch kernel, allocate memory, copy to device, copy back, free memory
Allocate host and device memory, copy data to device, launch kernel, copy result back, free memory
Copy data to device, free memory, allocate memory, launch kernel, copy back
Allocate device memory only, launch kernel, free memory
questions.explain: The standard CUDA program shape is: allocate host and device memory, copy input to the device, launch the kernel, copy the result back to the host, then free both allocations.

questions.q: When PyTorch code calls torch.matmul() on two CUDA tensors, what is happening underneath?
options: PyTorch is running the computation entirely on the CPU
PyTorch is launching a highly-tuned cuBLAS kernel on the device, the same conceptual model as a hand-written <<<...>>> kernel launch
PyTorch is compiling new CUDA code at runtime from scratch for every call
PyTorch avoids using the GPU for matrix multiplication
questions.explain: PyTorch's CUDA tensor operations like matmul launch pre-built, highly optimized cuBLAS kernels on the device — following the same host/device, kernel-launch model covered in this lesson, just hidden behind a Python API.
